title: fix(community-monitor): owner traffic is not evidence, deterministic relist, served-model notices
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Context: the monitor vetoed correct hides of chigwell models and asked for a manual relist because "real traffic is 100% ok". That traffic was the owner's own uptime monitor (`LLM7-monitoring` key, ~2 req/min per model, identical usage on every request). Every other caller has had 0% success on those models for 7 days, and the probe's 400 is the provider's own `model_unavailable`. The agent had written the exemption into its memory and applied it every cycle.

- Adds a caller split before any traffic rate counts: exclude the owner (`owner_user_id`) and the probe account; require ≥10 attributable final requests from ≥3 distinct callers. Owner or single-caller traffic never hides, vetoes, or relists.
- Replaces the two recovery paths with one deterministic gate: hidden ≥1h, three consecutive passing exact-ID probes on separate cycles spanning ≥90 min (failure/inconclusive resets), plus a non-owner traffic veto. Owner requests never shorten it. Audio/video/embeddings need 90% across ≥10 requests from ≥3 non-owner callers in two cycles.
- Forbids owner/model/provider exemptions in agent memory (the two poisoned notes were archived on the box today).
- Adds duty 2d: compares the model name each upstream writes into its stream with the declared `upstream_model` and measures fallback share; posts informational `MISMATCH` / `FALLBACK` panels tagging the owner so callers learn what actually answers them. Never hides or relists.
- `probe.mjs` records `servedModel` and gains `--models-file` for batch recovery probes; `chat-stream.mjs` returns the streamed model name; test added.

Verified: `node --test operations/community-monitor/*.test.mjs` (16 pass); live `--models-file` run against two hidden IDs; live `--model community/chigwell/llm7-fast` reports `servedModel: mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407` (an earlier run of the same listing streamed `codestral-latest`).

gist.headline: The garden gets receipts
gist.blurb: The model monitor now ignores a provider watering its own plants when judging whether the garden is healthy. Recovery is deterministic, and mismatched upstream answers get a polite little signpost.
gist.summary: Community model monitoring now excludes owner and probe traffic, requires at least 10 final requests from 3 non-owner callers for traffic evidence, and restores hidden models only after three passing exact-ID probes across 90 minutes plus non-owner validation.
gist.impact: Callers get more reliable model availability decisions, while new informational MISMATCH and FALLBACK notices reveal when an upstream serves a different model or falls back to another one.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden inspector using a clipboard and magnifying glass to check several code-plants. A CRT monitor robot compares each plant's labeled seed packet with the name shown on a tiny terminal stream, while three separate friendly visitor markers provide honest growth measurements; a small notice board reads MISMATCH / FALLBACK. This represents independent caller evidence, deterministic recovery checks, and transparent served-model reporting.
